Keep your salary. Your store starts with small tests on budgets you approve — nothing here bets the paycheck. [CLM-01.AV-04]
Before you pay you can read exactly what the $500 covers — and what it doesn't: product costs, platform fees and ad spend are yours, and you set the ad budget. [CLM-04.AV-02]
Sellers who find a product that sells usually tested five to ten first, each on a small budget. [CLM-02.AV-01]
The platform's own guide has store builders hand the store over "when it's ready to go live" — that's where most builders' job ends. [CLM-02.AV-07]
Getting stuck on the setup isn't about being smart. Capable people stall at exactly this step — the setup was never the part you needed to learn. [CLM-03.AV-03]
Products are released in stages, not one big drop, and chosen from search demand, seasonality and competition data — not by trying to out-price the big stores. [CLM-05.AV-07]
Your first store didn't prove online stores don't work for you — it got one try. [CLM-01.AV-01]
In a lot of the stories that went wrong, the store was built inside the builder's own account — and until it's handed over, the platform treats it as theirs. [CLM-02.AV-02]
The $500 build fee is refundable within 7 days — until you accept delivery or add any service. [CLM-07.AV-07]
You don't have to choose between doing it yourself and a $5,000–$20,000 agency: the first step is $500, published. [CLM-03.AV-07]
Your store is set up for you — payments, shipping, listings — and opened in your name. No more weeks in the settings. [CLM-04.AV-03]
Plenty of people lose money on a first store — and the ones who make it kept trying. [CLM-09.AV-01]
Hundreds of clicks and zero orders usually means the product didn't land, not that nobody came — the average Shopify store turns about 1 in 70 visits into a sale. [CLM-04.AV-01]
